headline: Approved funding for ecosystem services analysis and recommended approval of amended vegetation ordinance
summary: The board approved minutes from August 3, 2026 and approved a funding request for an ecosystem services analysis, which will move to the Board of Finance and City Council. The board also recommended approval of the amended vegetation ordinance, which will go to City Council for a first read on September 28. The rest of the meeting covered a retreat presentation and board discussion of priorities and passions.
decisions: Approved the August 3, 2026 minutes as written, 5-0-0.
Approved the funding request for the ecosystem services analysis, 8-0-0.
Recommended approval of the amended vegetation ordinance, 8-0-0.

Conservation Board Meeting Minutes 
Monday, September 14, 2026 – 5:00 pm 
In-Person Meeting 
 
Attendance   
 Board Members: Rebecca Roman (RR), Zoe Richards (ZR), Alan Reichard (AR), Ryan Crehan 
(RC), Dale Azaria (DA), Kelly Farrell (KF), Evan Horne (EH), Lee Toomey (LT) 
 Absent: None 
 Public: None 
 Staff: Scott Gustin (Permitting & Inspections), Dan Cahill, VJ Comai  (Parks & Rec), Dr. Kelli Perkins 
(REIB) 
 
RR, chair, called the meeting to order at 5:02 p.m.  
 
Minutes 
 
August 3, 2026 minutes 
 
A MOTION was made by DA and SECONDED by AR: 
 
Approve the minutes as written. 
 
Vote: 5-0-0, motion carried. (RC LT, KF not yet present)     
 
Public Comment 
 
None. 
 
Update & Discussion 
 
1. Ecosystem Services Analysis 
Consideration of ecosystem services analysis proposal and funding request 
 
RR overviewed the proposed analysis and why we’re pursuing it.  SG noted that the Parks & Recreation 
Commission voted to approve it last week, and he mentioned next steps with the Board of Finance and 
the City Council if the Conservation Board approves the request tonight.   
 
A MOTION was made by ZR and SECONDED by KF: 
 
Approve the funding request for the ecosystem services analysis. 
 
Vote: 8-0-0, motion carried.  
 
2. Draft amended vegetation ordinance 
Consideration of amended vegetation ordinance
Conservation Board Minutes 
September 14, 2026 - pg. 2 
   
 
Dan Cahill provided context and intent for the proposed vegetation ordinance amendment . 
 
SG presented slides outlining the major features of the amended ordinance.  He noted the draft ordinance 
will proceed to City Council for a first read on September 28 if the Conservation Board recommends 
approval tonight.   
 
DA noted that the amendment has come a long way since the initial draft.     
 
A MOTION was made by KF and SECONDED by DA: 
 
Recommend approval of the amended vegetation ordinance. 
 
Vote: 8-0-0, motion carried.  
 
Conservation Board Retreat 
 
Presentation by Dr. Kelli Perkins focused on outdoor spaces in America and follow up Board discussion.   
 
Following discussion of Dr. Perkins’ presentation and discussion, KF offered paw paw seedlings that 
she’s grown.   
 
RR overviewed board responsibilities and subcommittees.  Open Space Subcommittee meetings are 
hour-long work sessions open to any board member who’s interested in whatever is being worked on.  
The Long Range Planning Committee is tied to the Planning Commission and meets as-needed to talk 
long range items.   
 
Board members expressed interest in improving the format and facilitation of the annual joint meeting.  
 
RR noted additional work items that are underway: 
 
- Specimen tree map 
- Wetlands ordinance amendment 
- Legacy fund (funding and conservation infrastructure) 
- Vegetation ordinance 
- Ecosystem services assessment 
- Communications collaboration with Parks Communications staff 
RC noted shoreline standards that have been established 
 
KF, are there things we’d like to get ahead of?  RR, this is something to consider as part of the SWOT 
analysis.   
 
Board discussion: What’s your passion?   
 
DA, concern about climate change brought her into this realm.  Her passion is protecting Lake 
Champlain.  We need places to cool off, to protect our drinking water.   
 
AR wants to be proactive and work to fix things.  As an educator, he sees a lack of environmental 
education. Let’s help kids care about where they live.   
 
RC, the NNE schools and parks are close together, but there’s not much operational connection among 
them.  He’s interested in making those connections.
Conservation Board Minutes 
September 14, 2026 - pg. 3 
   
ZR, climate change is an area the Conservation Board can focus on supporting (native plants, nature 
connections for students).  What is our role in elevating nature based climate solution work?   
 
KF, the biodiversity crises.  It is just as dire but less reversible than the climate crisis.   
 
RC, make change part of the community fabric.   
 
EH noted some quick wins like listing out the local environmental organizations and what they’re up to.   
 
DA said she feels like she has capacity to help with the work of the Board outside of meetings.   
 
LT is super passionate about the non-human inhabitants of Burlington.  Interested in habitat protection 
and steering growth into appropriate locations.  Curious about community forest funding and how that 
might be leveraged towards conservation.   
 
RR summed up two broad themes: 1) Land protection and using the Board’s soft power 2) Place-based 
connections, land stewardship and connections.   
 
ZR, we can elevate the folks doing this work.   
 
Adjournment 
7:50 PM.
